issue: A link-rate unit slip: 'HDR InfiniBand delivers 200 GB/s per link (25 GB/s in both link coding; NDR doubles this to 400 GB/s)'. The parenthetical gives the correct payload figure (25 GB/s per direction after line coding), which corresponds to a 200 Gb/s raw link, not 200 GB/s. As printed, the sentence asserts a 200 GB/s link and then, in the same breath, a 25 GB/s payload — an 8x internal contradiction that a reader sizing links or NICs will trip over. The same slip repeats for NDR ('400 GB/s' for a 400 Gb/s link).
evidence: Printed 177: 'HDR InfiniBand delivers 200 GB/s per link (25 GB/s in both link coding; NDR doubles this to 400 GB/s).' 200 Gb/s x 64/66 = 193.9 Gb/s = 24.2 GB/s per direction, i.e. ~25 GB/s payload; bidirectional = ~50 GB/s. NDR 400 Gb/s -> ~50 GB/s per direction.
acceptance_test: The sentence reads 'HDR InfiniBand delivers 200 Gb/s per link (~25 GB/s per direction after line coding; NDR doubles this to 400 Gb/s, ~50 GB/s per direction)', and the per-direction and bidirectional figures are both stated so that the 40 GB/s multi-rail effective figure used in Fig 9.1 and in the worked example can be derived from it without ambiguity.

issue: The worked example attributes the multi-rail effective-throughput figure to '§9.2 and Fig 9.1', but Fig 9.1 is the eight-rank ring-traffic figure and Fig 9.2 is the four-rank SUM figure; the multi-rail 40 GB/s assumption is stated in the Fig 9.1 legend/caption, not in Fig 9.2. As printed the pointer sends the reader to a figure that does not contain the number, and to a section whose figure is about a different mechanism.
evidence: Printed 157: 'A realistic effective throughput is roughly 40 GB/s (aggregated across 2 HDR rails/ports per node — the multi-rail effective throughput referenced in §9.2 and Fig 9.1).' Fig 9.1 (printed 153) legend: 'Two-way HDR: assumed effective 40 GB/s'. Fig 9.2 (printed 154) contains no bandwidth figure.
acceptance_test: The parenthetical points to the location that actually states the 40 GB/s multi-rail assumption (Fig 9.1 and its caption, or the section that introduces it), and the section number matches the figure number it is paired with.

issue: The prose says the three patterns are shown 'side by side', but the figure stacks them vertically as panels A, B, and C.
evidence: Printed p. 166: 'Fig. 10.1 shows the three canonical patterns side by side.' Printed p. 174 repeats: 'Fig 10.1 illustrates the three canonical patterns — TP, PP, DP — side by side.' The rendered figure on p. 167 is a vertical stack: A above B above C.
acceptance_test: Either change both prose references to 'stacked' / 'in three panels' or redesign the figure so the three panels are genuinely side by side; then re-scan all references to Fig. 10.1 for the same wording.

issue: Panel B's layer split contradicts the prose that introduces it. The figure labels the stages 'layers 1-9', 'layers 10-19', 'layers 20-28' (a 28-layer model, 0-based GPU indexing), while the immediately preceding text (p.166, item 2) says 'GPU 1 runs layers 1-10, GPU 2 runs 11-20, and so on' (1-based, different boundaries). The canonical model used elsewhere in the book is 70B with 80 layers, so the drawn 28-layer stack is also inconsistent with the canonical configuration the caption invokes.
evidence: Rendered p.187 panel B: 'GPU 0 / layers 1-9', 'GPU 1 / layers 10-19', 'GPU 2 / layers 20-28'. Rendered p.166: 'Pipeline parallelism (PP) splits the model's layers (stages) across GPUs. GPU 1 runs layers 1-10, GPU 2 runs 11-20, and so on'. Rendered p.194: 'the canonical 70B fits across an 8xH100 node through intra-host model parallelism'.
acceptance_test: Make the figure's stage boundaries and GPU indexing match the prose exactly (same layer ranges, same GPU numbering convention), and make the total layer count consistent with the canonical 80-layer model, or relabel the panel explicitly as 'schematic: 28-layer toy model'.

issue: The bottom line in panel C is clipped at the right edge: 'throughput scales linearly until a shared resource binc'.
evidence: Rendered panel C reads: 'inference: independent replicas, no sync · throughput scales linearly until a shared resource binc'. The final word is cut off by the panel border.

issue: The caption asserts that replication is shown where it exists ('replication appears where it exists (TP's activations, DP's whole model)'), but TP activation replication is not drawn. Panel A shows only the sharded weight bar W0|W1 above the two GPUs; nothing indicates that the same activation tensor enters both GPUs. The caption therefore claims a visual element the figure does not contain.
evidence: Rendered p.187 panel A: a single hatched bar labelled 'one layer's weight matrix W' with W0 and W1, above 'GPU 0' and 'GPU 1'; the only inter-GPU mark is the red 'all-reduce partial sums -> full output' arrow. Caption: 'Each panel names what splits and what communicates; replication appears where it exists (TP's activations, DP's whole model).'
acceptance_test: Either add an activation-replication visual to panel A (e.g. an input activation arrow fanning to both GPUs, labelled 'activation replicated'), or amend the caption to state that TP activation replication is described in the text but not drawn.

issue: The panel names an 'idle (bubble) at fill/drain' but does not draw any bubble or idle slot, so the reader cannot see the pipeline bubble the caption claims is illustrated.
evidence: Panel B contains three GPU boxes and arrows, plus the text 'idle (bubble) at fill/drain — pipeline-wide'. No hatched, empty, or otherwise marked idle region appears. The caption says 'an idle bubble at fill/drain'.
acceptance_test: Add a visible idle slot/bubble at the pipeline fill and drain (or a bracket showing the bubble), or remove the bubble claim from the panel and caption.

issue: Panel B asserts a pipeline bubble but never depicts one. The label 'idle (bubble) at fill/drain - pipeline-wide' has no anchor in the drawing (no empty slot, no gap, no unfilled stage), and the caption's microbatch claim ('the PP bubble size depends on microbatch scheduling (more microbatches shrink the bubble but add memory)') has no visual support. The label also appears to start at or on the panel's rounded-rectangle border, with no leader.
evidence: Rendered p.187 panel B: three orange GPU boxes in a row connected by red arrows, with 'activations -> P2P at stage boundaries' above and 'idle (bubble) at fill/drain - pipeline-wide' below-left, positioned at the panel's left border; no bubble region is drawn anywhere in the panel.
acceptance_test: Add a visual bubble (e.g. an empty/dimmed stage slot during fill, or a timeline strip showing microbatches and the idle interval) with a leader from the label, and move the label clear of the panel border; confirm at 100% print size that the label does not touch the frame.

issue: The caption says replication appears where it exists, including 'TP's activations', but panel A does not show replicated activations; it shows only split weights and partial sums.
evidence: Caption: 'replication appears where it exists (TP's activations, DP's whole model).' Panel A shows a split weight matrix W, two GPUs, and an all-reduce box; no replicated activation tensor is drawn.
acceptance_test: Add a small 'same activations' indicator on both TP GPUs, or revise the caption so it does not claim the figure shows TP activation replication.

issue: The caption conflates a sequence with a slot: 'each row is one sequence (slot) evolving over time'. In continuous batching a row is a slot that can host successive sequences, which is exactly what the green backfill blocks depict.
evidence: Caption: 'each row is one sequence (slot) evolving over time'. The right panel shows a row with blue, then green, then blue, i.e. a slot reused by more than one sequence.
acceptance_test: Change to 'each row is one slot; a slot may host successive sequences over time' and check the surrounding prose for the same sequence/slot conflation.

issue: The discrete panel contradicts its own annotation: all four rows show an identical blue 'sequence in flight' block of the same width, so no sequence finishes before the others, yet the note states 'GPU slots idle (pink) when a sequence finishes early'. The pink region therefore has no depicted cause and the reader cannot see the phenomenon the figure exists to illustrate.
evidence: Rendered p.200, discrete panel: four rows, each with an equal-width blue block at the left followed by an equal-length pink block; all four rows terminate at the same x. Figure note: 'GPU slots idle (pink) when a sequence finishes early'. Caption: 'a batch is locked until its slowest member finishes, so short outputs idle in the ... slots'.
acceptance_test: Redraw the discrete panel so at least one row's blue block ends earlier than the batch's end (e.g. staggered blue widths, one short sequence), so the pink tail is visibly caused by an early finisher; or, if the intent is that all sequences finish together, replace the note with wording that matches the drawing.

issue: The green blocks are not explained as the first decode step of a backfilled sequence; because they are followed by blue blocks, a reader can plausibly infer that green is a separate short sequence that ends and is replaced by another blue sequence.
evidence: Legend: blue = 'sequence in flight', green = 'new sequence (backfill)'. The top row shows blue, then green, then blue. The caption says only 'new sequences (green) snap into freed slots' and does not say green marks only the first step.
acceptance_test: Add a note or label stating that green marks the first decode step of a backfilled sequence and that the following blue is the same sequence continuing; or redraw so the entire backfilled sequence is visually identified.
